newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hebron Jews protest against Palestinian market.
newsitem.headline: Hebron Jews protest against Palestinian market.

text.p: Jews and Arabs hurled oranges and abuse at each other in Hebron on Thursday as Jewish settlers protested against an Israeli decision to reopen an Arab produce market in the volatile West Bank town, witnesses said.
Witnesses said scuffles and shouting matches erupted in Hebron's heart after about 15 Jewish settlers marched on the newly reopened market they say endangers their security.
They said the shouts were soon drowned out by a barrage of citrus.

Israeli soldiers, who earlier on Thursday stopped settlers from marching on the market which abuts a Jewish enclave in the city centre, cleared the area of Palestinians and allowed only municipal employees to stay near the stores.
"We came to open our stores but the soldiers stopped us from going inside," said Hassan Dais, who owns a shop in the market.
An Israeli army spokeswoman said the soldiers escorted the settlers away. Palestinians said settlers were trying to stop merchants from cleaning and renovating stores in the market.
Israel partly reopened the market on Wednesday three years after closing it in the wake of a settler massacre of 29 Palestinian worshippers at Hebron's al-Ibrahimi mosque.
The Jewish state agreed to reopen the market after handing over 80 percent of Hebron, home to 400 Jews and more than 100,000 Arabs, to Palestinian self-rule last month under a U.S.-brokered deal.
The market is in the 20 percent of the city that remains under Israeli control.
